reviewer: Claude review agent (independent of the extractor); no human review claimed
scope: Independent review of the 94 records of the BioEmu-2 batch (13 sources, 1 model, 5 configurations, 75 claims, no evaluations and no results) by a different agent from the extractor, against the extraction frozen at batch.jsonl SHA-256 4e40c0c17e77b781c00b90eb27d48e25dd24aff077f650901762a3c63e4bf516. No vocabulary concept is added and data/vocab is untouched. All thirteen artifacts were re-retrieved from the URLs their source records record, and every SHA-256 matched the source record; every archived gzip under artifacts/ decompresses to bytes with the same SHA-256, so the archive is provably the retrieved bytes. The mutable Hugging Face API listing also matched at review time, its counters unchanged at downloads 0 and likes 25, which is not expected to hold at a later retrieval. npm run batch -- check-values was not run and no value-check.tsv exists: the batch holds no result, so there is no printed value to locate. Instead all 75 claims were checked at their own source_locator in the re-retrieved bytes, in three passes. First, the two model-card tables were parsed again by a reviewer script from the re-retrieved file, without using extract/parse_model_card.py: all nine model summary rows and all twelve training data rows map one to one onto claims and every cell matches, with no table row and no summary row left unclaimed. Second, every claim sentence was matched mechanically against the normalised artifact text of its own sources; 42 of the 75 claims matched their source word for word, and the other 33 were listed and read by eye at their locator. Thirteen of those 33 are model-card table cells reflowed into prose, which the table parse above had already cleared cell by cell; the remaining 20 join two printed sentences, strip markdown links or code spans, or respell an en dash, a micro sign or a multiplication sign, and each one's wording was compared with the printed text. Third, every ordinal locator was counted against the artifact. Five locators were corrected, all pointing at the wrong sentence, paragraph or heading rather than carrying a wrong fact, and the corrections are in review/apply-review.py and in the dated review. The absence of a numeric evaluation value was confirmed independently by reading all thirteen artifacts and grepping them for the metric names the model card's evaluation methodology uses: the four evaluation settings are described in prose with no figure, and the two context-parallel throughput plots are linked images, so no evaluation or result record is owed. The store was grepped again for BioEmu under any spelling and holds none, so the absent family link is right. The eight questions the extractor raised are ruled on in docs/reviews/2026-11-15-bioemu2.md with the deciding source text; none required a record to be added or removed. Every record's review object was replaced with this pass's method, reviewer, date and notes, keeping the extractor's transcription note under an Extraction: prefix; no value, ID, link, status or source hash was changed.
limitations: Automated review by a Claude agent, independent of the extractor but not human scientific review. Transcription was checked against the pinned bytes; nothing was reproduced, no model was run and no value was recomputed.

The batch holds no evaluation and no result, because no pinned artifact prints a numeric evaluation value. The model card describes four evaluation settings without a single figure, so BioEmu-2 enters the store with descriptive claims only and supports no comparison with any other model.

No paper, preprint or technical report for BioEmu-2 was retrievable by 2026-11-15, so every claim rests on the developer's own repository and model card. The review repeated the extractor's checks that the pinned tree has no CITATION file and the model card cites no publication, but did not repeat the literature search.

The 2,047,661,181 byte checkpoint was not downloaded. checkpoint_sha256 holds the digest the publisher serves, which the Git LFS pointer and the Hugging Face API listing for the same revision both state identically; weights_sha256 stays unextracted. Hashing the bytes locally is a gap for a batch that runs the model.

The model card and the README at the same commit do not agree on the smallest tested GPU. Both statements are kept as separate claims with their own locators and subjects, the conflict is described in the runtime configuration's accelerator_details, and no minimum device is asserted on the model. No evidence concern was added: nothing in the store rests on either claim, and neither artifact prints a memory figure that a comparison could use.

The folding evaluation names the Boltz-1 test set with no version, split or target count and no baseline, so no protocol was created and reported-dataset-e45a5a140888ee was not linked. The store's own record for that dataset carries version, split and accession as unextracted, so linking it would assert an identity neither source fixes.

The model stays at family level. The model card prints no version row and says the same checkpoint was used for every benchmark without naming it, so the evaluated checkpoint is not assigned to bioemu2-preview; missing_metadata.checkpoint_revision records that.

Four of the five README key-features bullets are recorded as claims. The second bullet, equilibrium sampling and structure prediction from the command line or Python, has no claim of its own; the review left it so, because the two mode configurations and claim-two-trained-tasks carry that fact with their own locators. notes.md speaks of five bullets and overstates by one.
build.py reproduces the extraction state of batch.jsonl, not the reviewed state. review/apply-review.py turns the first into the second and is the record of what the review changed.
